anya: Heads-up — prod-cu1 showed a sudden throughput drop ~09:06 UTC. P99 latency spiked, several inference workers restarted, and we saw OOM churn on a subset of nodes.
matt: Confirmed on our side. Grafana shows GPU mem usage stable then a step increase and repeated worker restarts. KV cache eviction rate jumped ~8x at the same time: https://grafana.redwood/prod/cu1/d/xyz
infra-bot: alert: node gpu-34 - worker_restart_count >= 3 in 5m (detected at 09:07:12)
kai: Quick profiler dump: kernel-selection logs indicate many fallbacks from fast-quantized -> fallback_kernel when allocator returns ENOMEM on slab allocs. Small batches (1-2 tokens) disproportionately hit the fallback path. Snippet:```kernel_select: model=redwood-v2q batch=1 seq=64 cores=1 selected=fast_q fallback=fallback_kernel reason=slab_alloc_fail```
samir: Hypothesis: noisy tenant caused allocation churn -> fragmentation -> subsequent small-batch requests trigger expensive kernel paths and then OOMs. If KV cache evicts aggressively it amplifies allocation pressure.
matt: Tried isolating the tenant by tainting their pool at 09:12, but restarts continued for ~4m after. Replayed load in staging and reproduced restarts within 2-3m using a small-batch-heavy replay.
anya: Profile numbers pasted from the trace: batch_distribution: 1:62%, 2:20%, 4:8%, >=8:10%. kernel_fallback_count=6200 over 6m window. p99 latency +420ms vs baseline.
devon: Allocator log shows sweep latency spikes right before restarts: "sweep: duration=87ms unclaimed=12 slabs fragmented=47" repeated. That aligns with fragmentation causing synchronous slow paths.
kai: Mitigation proposal: 1) Increase KV cache reserved headroom by 15% to reduce eviction cascade; 2) Adjust batching heuristic to wait up to 15ms if GPU is idle and small-batch fraction >40% (to coalesce). Suggest canary on 3 nodes.
samir: Also worth checking last week's scheduler tweak (scheduler v2.3.1) that lowered preemption thresholds — could have increased noisy-tenant pressure. Can we roll that back on canary if needed?
matt: ops-bot: starting canary rollout (commit abc123) to nodes [gpu-33,gpu-35,gpu-36] with increased kv-reserve + batching-wait=15ms. Link: https://deploys.redwood/abc123
infra-bot: Canary metrics: within 7m of rollout, kernel_fallback_count on canary nodes down 78%, worker restarts stopped, throughput recovered to baseline. Marking incident state: mitigated. Further postmortem scheduled.
anya: TL;DR: noisy tenant -> allocator fragmentation -> KV eviction cascade -> kernel fallback for small batches -> OOMs and restarts. Canary changes (kv headroom + small wait batching) mitigated. Postmortem will recommend long-term: allocator sweep tuning, batching heuristic permanent tweak, and scheduler preemption revert if we still see pressure. :white_check_mark:
